c.tagline: Romantic Germany distilled — a castle ruin, the oldest university, and the Neckar valley.

taxi.fareNote: Fares are metered and regulated; you can hail on the street, wait at a rank, or book by phone or app. Ride-hailing apps FreeNow, Uber and Bolt also operate.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number for ambulance and fire; 110 reaches the police. Both are free and staffed by English-speaking operators.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Petty pickpocketing can occur in the Hauptstrasse tourist crowds and around Bismarckplatz and the main station late at night.

hood_desc: Heidelberg's postcard old town: a long pedestrian spine of Renaissance and baroque houses running from Bismarckplatz to the Karlstor, beneath the red-sandstone castle ruins and beside the Old Bridge over the Neckar. Home to the Marktplatz, the Church of the Holy Spirit and the historic university quarter; best for first-timers who want every sight on foot.

A leafy, affluent residential district across the Neckar reached by the Old Bridge, with elegant villas, the start of the Philosophers' Walk (Philosophenweg) and its river-and-castle views, plus quiet cafes; suits travellers who want calm, greenery and the classic panorama of the old town.

A convenient quarter just west of the old town around the main hospitals and Bergheimer Strasse, within walking distance of both the Altstadt and the train station and lined with mid-range and chain hotels; a practical, well-connected base.

An elegant late-19th-century grid of stucco townhouses, tree-lined streets and squares between the old town and the station — one of Germany's best-preserved Gruenderzeit quarters — with local cafes and a residential feel; good for a quieter, characterful stay near the centre.

A modern, car-light passivhaus district built on former rail land west of the station, with new-build apartments, wide green promenades, cinemas and family amenities; the most contemporary and affordable area, handy for the Hauptbahnhof but a tram ride from the old town.
lodging: House of Hütter – Heidelberg Suites & Spa

water.note: Tap water is excellent and safe to drink everywhere.

transit.hours: Trams and buses run roughly 5am to around 1am; a Moonliner night-bus network covers weekend nights.
transit.pay: No tap-in gates: buy tickets in the RNV/VRN app, at machines, or from the driver, and validate before boarding; one ticket covers RNV trams and buses across the VRN network. A single ride in Heidelberg is about €3 (~$3.20) and a day ticket about €7.50. Staying weeks? The €58/month Deutschland-Ticket covers local transit nationwide. The Bergbahn funicular up to the castle and Königstuhl is priced separately.

tip.r: Service is included by law; locals round the bill up to the next euro or add about 5-10% for good service, handed to the server rather than left on the table.

landmarks: Heidelberg Castle (Heidelberger Schloss)
Europe's most romantic ruin looms in red sandstone above the Neckar, its Renaissance facades, Great Vat wine barrel and gardens inspiring poets for centuries.
Old Bridge (Karl-Theodor-Brücke)
This graceful 18th-century sandstone bridge with its twin-towered medieval gate and bronze monkey statue frames the classic view of castle, river and old town.
Philosophers' Way (Philosophenweg)
The scenic hillside path where university thinkers once strolled delivers Heidelberg's definitive panorama of castle and spires across the Neckar, prettiest at golden hour.
Old Town and Hauptstraße
One of Europe's longest pedestrian streets threads a baroque old town rebuilt after 1693, lined with student pubs, boutiques and centuries-old chocolatiers.
Church of the Holy Spirit (Heiliggeistkirche)
Gothic hall church at the Marktplatz's heart, once split between Catholics and Protestants, whose tower gallery surveys the old town's sea of red rooftops.
Königstuhl Summit and Funicular
Ride one of Germany's oldest funiculars past the castle to this 568-meter peak for forest trails, a falconry center and vast Rhine plain views.
Heidelberg University and Old Assembly Hall (Alte Aula)
Germany's oldest university, founded 1386, welcomes visitors to its sumptuous neo-Renaissance ceremonial hall and the University Museum in the baroque Old University.
Student Jail (Studentenkarzer)
Graffiti-covered cells where mischievous students were locked up until 1914 preserve silhouette portraits and witty inscriptions, a beloved quirk of university history.
Marktplatz and Kornmarkt
Heidelberg's twin baroque squares pair the Hercules Fountain and town hall with the Kornmarkt Madonna, offering the old town's loveliest castle-backed photo compositions.
Thingstätte and Heiligenberg
Atop the Holy Mountain, an eerie 1935 amphitheater and the ruined St. Michael's Monastery reward hikers with history and views over the Neckar valley.

intl.to: Singen & Zurich (Switzerland) - via Stuttgart on the Gaubahn

train.note: Heidelberg Hauptbahnhof is about 1.5 km west of the Altstadt, with frequent trams and buses to Bismarckplatz and Universitatsplatz. Almost every ICE and IC line through the Rhine-Neckar calls here, but the only regular through cross-border service is the IC 87 Gaubahn train towards Singen and Zurich; for France, Belgium and the Netherlands you change at Mannheim, five minutes away, which is a full high-speed hub with TGV and ICE International departures. Frankfurt Airport is under an hour by direct IC/ICE, which is usually simpler than flying into Stuttgart. Cross-border fares are best bought as a single Sparpreis Europa ticket from int.bahn.de rather than leg by leg.

intl.to: France, the Netherlands, Czechia & across Europe

bus.note: Long-distance coaches stop at the bus terminal on the north side of Heidelberg Hauptbahnhof, a short walk from the tram stops. FlixBus is effectively the only operator and tickets are online only in practice. Frankfurt is about 1h15 by coach and Munich roughly 4h30; for most European destinations you will change in Frankfurt or Mannheim, both under an hour away.

ferry.note: Heidelberg is well inland on the Neckar and has no ferry service in the transport sense. Excursion boats do run up the Neckar from the landing stages by the Stadthalle below the Old Bridge to Neckargemund, Neckarsteinach and Hirschhorn between spring and autumn, and a small solar-powered passenger ferry crosses the river at Neckarhausen; for sea crossings the nearest ports are Rotterdam and Hamburg.

half.name: Speyer
half.blurb: Cathedral city on the Rhine with a Romanesque imperial cathedral holding the tombs of Salian and Hohenstaufen emperors.

half.name: Mannheim
half.blurb: Baroque-planned city built on a grid of numbered squares, with a palace and a Rhine-Neckar river confluence.

half.name: Worms
half.blurb: Rhine city where Luther defended his teachings before the 1521 Diet, with one of Germany's oldest Jewish cemeteries.

full.name: Strasbourg
full.blurb: Alsatian city on the French-German border, with a pink sandstone cathedral and a canal-laced old quarter.
